# Inside the Aḗr restoration: what the marks recover
The domain you're reading about exists because someone refused to let **Aḗr** stay *aer*.

Aḗr has no mythic biography; its story is the history of Greek thought. From Homer to Aristotle, it moves from mere atmosphere to a recognized element of the cosmos. In Homer, aēr is the lower, misty air where mortals breathe and battle; aithēr is the bright upper air of the gods.  The distinction sets up a cosmic hierarchy: the higher the air, the more divine it is.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Aḗr
- **ASCII form:** aer
- **Meaning:** "Air, mist"
- **Domain of influence:** Air
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ἀήρ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 6 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἀήρ**. On the evidence, it means "Air, mist".

**Aḗr** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *aer* and **Aḗr** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Aḗr** lives at [/sites/aer/](/sites/aer/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/aer/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/aer/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/aer/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Aḗr** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Aviation & Aerospace** — The lower air itself — the misty atmosphere between earth and the bright aithēr above; the medium every aircraft breathes.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — Environmental science treats air as a global commons; the atmosphere under policy is his body.
- **Meteorology & Weather Intelligence** — Weather is his element in motion; every forecast samples the moving air.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
